clue.text: Port to share out

definitions.meaning: A port city on the Croatian coast of the Adriatic
to divide something up among people, as in splitting the bill

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a Croatian harbour city, and the verb for dividing a total between several people.

clue.text: SW toff beginning to sample the fury of the bank manager?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word sample is its opening letter only

parts.note: a whimsical name for someone whose job is lending money, one who loans
fury is rage, intense anger

explanation.surface: A posh young man starts to taste the wrath of his bank manager.
explanation.walkthrough: SW is the postcode area of south-west London, home of Chelsea's Sloane Square, so an SW toff is a fashionable posh type from there. The pieces join in the order bank manager then fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stereotype of a well-off young Chelsea socialite, named after Sloane Square in the SW postcode area.

clue.text: Is one prone to accept fine? His punishment much worse!

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the fine letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: one prone is someone who lies down, a lier
F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person lying low will pay a fine, then notes a far harsher sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it describes a prisoner serving a life sentence, whose penalty is far worse than any fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner given a life sentence suffers a penalty far heavier than paying money to the court.

clue.text: Doctor inserted end of needle to soften flesh

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of inserted are rearranged
the end of needle is its final letter

explanation.surface: A physician pushes in a needle to make tissue softer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun for the person with the needle, but it is the anagram signal working on 'inserted' (giving TENDERIS).
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks beat or marinate meat to make it less tough, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Dead elephantine mammal in mother's wardrobe?

parts.note: mother is MA, and the possessive adds an S
a wardrobe holds the clothes one has to don, read whimsically as 'to don'

explanation.surface: An extinct beast is apparently lurking among Mum's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stretch: Ma's wardrobe is what Ma has 'to don', that is, to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: This prehistoric relative of elephants has been extinct for thousands of years, hence a dead elephantine animal.

clue.text: Uprising amounting to nothing? That's fine!

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a total of zero is a nil sum

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a rebellion that achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it is a cotton fabric, and the clue says 'that is fine' because it is a fine, thin weave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine, lightly woven cotton cloth, so the material is something that is fine.

clue.text: One's blooming meat sauce!

clue.text: Short, extremely cold clothing for king in dance

explanation.definitionFit: A lively Bohemian dance in duple time, popular in nineteenth-century ballrooms.

clue.text: Meat one found in the tail

clue.text: Monster with an iron stomach getting free meal

clue.text: So one can is red, or tin curiously orange at first
